The frontispiece, which the book places at page 128, is shown on the title page.
summary: F. Trench Townshend, a captain in the 2nd Life Guards, left Liverpool with a brother officer on 1 August 1868 for five months in North America. They saw New York, Newport, and Boston, camped and travelled by canoe in the Adirondacks, visited Montreal and Quebec, and went from Washington to the battlefields round Richmond and Petersburg. In the West, with the leave of Generals Sherman and Augur, they rode with an army scouting party across the plains of Nebraska and Kansas, while the United States was at war with the Sioux and Arapahoes, hunting buffalo and antelope.

They hunted elk and mountain sheep in the Rocky Mountains beyond Laramie, called on Brigham Young at Salt Lake City, crossed the desert and Nevada to San Francisco, and came home by Acapulco, Panama, Jamaica, and St. Thomas through a gale in the Atlantic. The book ends with a list of the animals they shot.
